description:
The ELSE of the plaintext password comparison at app/cbl/COSGN00C.cbl:241-246, and the one assertion in this set that the arm itself makes visible: this is the only rejecting path in the program that leaves WS-ERR-FLG alone. The typed user id addresses a row that exists, so EXEC CICS READ at :211-219 reports RESP 0 and :222 selects the found arm; SEC-USR-PWD then does not equal WS-USER-PWD at :223, so control takes the ELSE. In source order: EVALUATE TRUE at :117-130 falls through to WHEN OTHER CONTINUE at :128-129 because neither field is blank, :132-136 upper-cases both (an identity move here, since both are typed in upper case, which is what keeps this case about the comparison and not about the normalisation), :138 finds NOT ERR-FLG-ON and performs READ-USER-SEC-FILE, and :242-243 moves 'Wrong Password. Try again ...' into WS-MESSAGE, :244 moves -1 into PASSWDL and :245 paints the screen. The password typed is eight upper-case characters, exactly the width of the PIC X(08) it is compared against, so the mismatch is unambiguously a value mismatch and not an artefact of length or of case; case15 holds the same comparison to a strict prefix of the seeded value and case18 holds the key width, and neither is what this case is for.

THE PRESERVED ASYMMETRY. :241-246 moves the message, moves the cursor and sends the map, and it does NOT contain MOVE 'Y' TO WS-ERR-FLG. Every other rejecting path in the program does: the invalid-key arm at :92, the blank user id at :119, the blank password at :124, the not-found arm at :248 and the unexpected-response arm at :253. This one alone leaves the flag at the SET ERR-FLG-OFF of :75, so WS-ERR-FLG still reads 'N' when the task ends. The omission changes no outcome, because :138 - the program's only reader of the flag - has already been evaluated by the time :241 is reached, and that is exactly why it is worth pinning: an inconsistency that changes nothing is the kind a translation harmonises for tidiness, and preserving legacy behaviour means preserving it including its defects. It is a verified property of the source, not a transcription slip, and it is not to be corrected for consistency. The flag is not a CARDDEMO-COMMAREA field and so has no place in this fixture's payload; what pins it is the arm this case selects, which the gate reads back from the outcome and requires to carry the flag off.

No role and no next program, stated positively rather than left to omission. The EXEC CICS XCTL at :231-239 sits inside the true branch of :223 and is not reached, so the response names no program, no role is established and the termination is the EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID at :98-102 rather than a transfer. The row read is an administrator's - SEC-USR-TYPE is 'A' at offset 56 of row two - and CDEMO-USER-TYPE still comes back holding the 'U' it arrived with, because :227 moves the record's type into it only on the signing-on path. An administrator whose password fails is not an administrator to this program, and this case names neither of the two menu programs that :232 and :237 would otherwise have reached.

The communication area on a rejecting path, which is the statelessness assertion in its strongest form. Fifteen of the sixteen CARDDEMO-COMMAREA fields of app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy:19-44 come back exactly as they arrived; the one exception is CDEMO-USER-ID, written unconditionally by :134 before the read, which is why it leaves holding the typed ADMIN003 rather than the OLDUSER1 it arrived with. Thirteen of the fifteen arrive non-blank - the target transaction and program, the user type, the program context, the customer identifier and all three names, the account identifier and status, the card number and the last map and mapset - so the pass-through is asserted against real values rather than against blanks, which is what a case arriving with an empty area cannot do. CDEMO-FROM-TRANID and CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM arrive blank and leave blank, because :224-225 write them on the signing-on path only. A translation holding any of this in a session rather than carrying it in the payload would have nothing to hand back, and the thirteen would return empty.

USRSEC is seeded from app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:35-44, whose ten in-stream rows are 57 characters where app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy:17-23 declares 80: SEC-USR-ID X(08) at 0, SEC-USR-FNAME X(20) at 8, SEC-USR-LNAME X(20) at 28, SEC-USR-PWD X(08) at 48, SEC-USR-TYPE X(01) at 56 - which is 57 - then SEC-USR-FILLER X(23) at 57, which is 80. The 23-byte shortfall is supplied once at seed time by the declared USRSEC_FILLER_PAD_57_TO_80 normalisation and is never hand-padded into the rows. The same job corroborates the target width twice, with DCB=(LRECL=80,RECFM=FB) on SYSUT2 and RECORDSIZE(80,80) KEYS(8,0) on the cluster it loads. Row two, the row the typed key addresses, is pinned twice over: by all six named fields, so the diff is field for field, and by the complete 80-character image, so the total width is asserted too and a record that omitted SEC-USR-FILLER would be short by exactly 23. The record was read, so its decoded field set belongs to the observation even though the authentication failed. The dataset is addressed by its binding key USRSEC - the CICS file name at :39 and the FILE definition at app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD:88-95 - and never by a dataset name. expectedWrites is empty as a positive assertion: COSGN00C contains no WRITE, REWRITE or DELETE on any path, and the read at :211-219 does not specify UPDATE, so it takes no lock and holds no record. expectedReturnCode is 0 because grep -c RETURN-CODE over the program is 0; a wrong password does not change it.

The message and the screen. The literal at :242-243 is 29 characters - the COBOL statement is continued across two source lines but the literal is one string - and it travels through WS-MESSAGE PIC X(80) at :38, where it is space-padded, into ERRMSGO PIC X(78) by the MOVE at :149, where it is truncated on the right, because a COBOL MOVE into a PIC X receiver justifies left and truncates right. Two spaces are lost and none of the literal is, so ERRMSGO holds the 29 characters followed by 49 spaces. SEND-SIGNON-SCREEN at :145-157 is performed, so all eleven named items of mapset COSGN00 are pinned at the widths app/cpy-bms/COSGN00.CPY:86-152 declares them: TRNNAMEO X(4), TITLE01O X(40), CURDATEO X(8), PGMNAMEO X(8), TITLE02O X(40), CURTIMEO X(9), APPLIDO X(8), SYSIDO X(8), USERIDO X(8), PASSWDO X(8) and ERRMSGO X(78). USERIDO and PASSWDO carry the typed values straight back: this path performs no MOVE LOW-VALUES - only the cold start at :81 does - and COSGN0AO REDEFINES COSGN0AI at :85, so what was received occupies the same offsets that are sent. :244 requests the cursor on PASSWDL, the length item of the field at fault, which is carried as validation and highlight metadata rather than as a payload member, exactly as app/cpy-bms/COSGN00.CPY's xxxL, xxxF and xxxA items are throughout, so the cursor returns to the password rather than to the user id and no other length item is repositioned.

Determinism and the two substitutions. POPULATE-HEADER-INFO opens with MOVE FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE TO WS-CURDATE-DATA at :179, so the clock is pinned rather than read: 2022-07-19T23:12:33, traceable to this program's own version footer at :259 and expressed as a fixed local date-time so no timezone can shift it. Through app/cpy/CSDAT01Y.cpy, WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY is MM '/' DD '/' YY with YY taken from WS-CURDATE-YEAR(3:2), giving CURDATEO exactly 07/19/22 at its PIC X(8); WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS is HH ':' MM ':' SS, eight bytes, moved into CURTIMEO which app/cpy-bms/COSGN00.CPY:122 declares PIC X(9) - hence 23:12:33 followed by exactly one trailing space. Note that width: the sibling COUSR02 map declares its CURTIMEO PIC X(8) and the two must not be conflated. APPLID and SYSID come from EXEC CICS ASSIGN at :198-204, which has no Java equivalent and which neither application.yml nor application-test.yml binds, so CICSAWS1 and AWS1 space-padded to PIC X(8) are pinned constants standing in for those two calls; all twenty cases use the same pair, and the substitution is stated rather than hidden. The charset is named US-ASCII explicitly, because the nine ASCII fixtures are US-ASCII and the platform default is never relied on.

Two deviations recorded rather than quietly worked around. First, app/cbl/COSGN00C.cbl:59 is *COPY DFHATTR. with the asterisk in column 7, which makes it a COBOL comment, so no DFHATTR attribute constant applies to this program however many other programs copy that member. Second, COSGN00C never copies CSSETATY - its only consumer is COACTUPC - so there is no DFHRED plus '*' highlight applied at run time and no xxxC, xxxP, xxxH or xxxV item is assigned anywhere; the attributes map is empty for that reason and not for want of looking. The error emphasis is instead the PASSWDL cursor request plus the field's own static COLOR=RED with ATTRB=(ASKIP,BRT,FSET), assembled into the map once at app/bms/COSGN00.bms:197-200 and never assigned by the program. Where a run-time attribute value would come from is common/BmsAttributes, which reproduces DFHBMSCA and DFHATTR from IBM CICS documentation because both are IBM-supplied and absent from this checkout, as DFHAID is too - which is also why the attention identifier is named here by its common/CicsAid mnemonic DFHENTER and never as a raw byte.

The security posture is unchanged in both directions. :223 compares SEC-USR-PWD against WS-USER-PWD in plaintext, eight characters against eight, and this case drives the negative side of that comparison with nothing interposed on either side: the stored span is neither digested nor derived nor rewritten, and no credential store, no issued session credential and no security filter chain appears anywhere in it. That is an inherited property of the legacy design and an explicit non-goal of this migration, not something to correct here: digesting the stored span would reject every seeded row and change the observable behaviour. One further inherited property is visible in the message itself - 'Wrong Password. Try again ...' tells the caller that the user id was valid, where the not-found arm at :249 answers 'User not found. Try again ...' instead. That distinction is an information disclosure the program makes, preserved deliberately because the message text is observable output, and recorded here so that it is visible rather than buried, not because it is endorsed.

Provenance. Every expected value above is statically derived - by structured reading of app/cbl/COSGN00C.cbl cross-checked against app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy for the record layout, app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy for the communication area, app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy for the two titles, whose line 21 is commented out so that line 22 is the active CCDA-TITLE02, app/cpy/CSDAT01Y.cpy for the header, app/cpy-bms/COSGN00.CPY with app/bms/COSGN00.bms for the screen field shapes, app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD for transaction CC00 and the USRSEC file, and app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:35-44 for the ten seed rows. It was never captured from a live COBOL execution, which is empirically impossible in this environment: there is no z/OS or CICS runtime, the available compiler reports its indexed file handler disabled, no Language Environment CEE* services exist, and DFHAID, DFHBMSCA and DFHATTR are absent from the repository. Only the provenance of the expected values is substituted; the twenty cases, the field-for-field diffing and the diff-count-equals-zero gate all stand.

The unit is SignOnService, driven as a plain object with a fixture-backed SecUserRepository, and the eleven-item screen is projected by SignOnController, also a plain object - no MockMvc, no HTTP, no servlet container and no JobLauncher in the path. Exactly one keyed read is performed, the one at :211-219, and it addresses row two. All conversation state travels in the payload, so no server-side session exists to hold any of it. Neither the backward-GO TO restructuring gate nor the abend gate applies: grep -c "GO TO" and grep -c CEE3ABD over app/cbl/COSGN00C.cbl are both 0, and neither is faked; DUPKEY, DUPREC and ENDFILE are unreachable from this program, which performs one read and no write.
